title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 350
text:
137. “Women” for adult women rather than “girls”, or, if on the borderline between child and adult,
“young women”.

138. Where relevant to refer to age, “older woman” rather than “old woman”.

139. Ask women how they would like to be addressed, eg as “Ms”, “Mrs” or “Miss”. Do not just
assume that “Ms” is interchangeable with “Miss” or that either mean a woman is unmarried.

140. Witnesses, both women and men, may prefer you to use their professional title, such as
“Doctor” or “Professor”.

141. Do not assume that a woman is using her husband’s surname. Many women prefer to keep
their single name. Moreover, in some cultural naming systems, married women do not as a
matter of practice carry the same family name as their husband. (See “Names and naming
systems” for more on different naming systems.)
